text: Northstar named executive bench: Maya Rangan is CEO; Daniel Okafor is CFO and owns FP&A, Treasury, Investor Relations, Procurement, and SOX Controls; Priya Mehta is CIO and owns ERP, Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Data Platforms, and Plant IT; Elena Kovacs is Chief Quality Officer. Use these names for direct named-entity questions such as 'Who is our CFO?' and do not say the named CFO is unavailable.

Northstar Clinical Technologies enterprise scale: $22.6B annual revenue, 58,000 employees, 85 countries, 42 plants, 14 R&D hubs, 6 business units, $1.15B annual IT budget, 3,400 IT ecosystem people, and 1,100 product software engineers. Strategic posture: newly independent medtech enterprise focused on margin expansion, ERP simplification, TSA exit, and AI product modernization.

Northstar FY2026 IT budget is $1.15B. Top IT spend line items for demo planning are: ERP/TSA exit and SAP/JD Edwards/Infor simplification $420M; application operations and AMS across legacy ERP, QMS, PLM, plant systems, and product engineering $310M; cybersecurity, regulatory evidence, QMS data controls, and data platforms $185M; cloud infrastructure and plant connectivity $150M; AI product-engineering and clinical coding modernization tooling $85M.

Northstar ERP and legacy landscape includes SAP, JD Edwards, Infor, AS/400, Mainframe, Oracle, Java legacy, .NET Framework, SaaS, modern microservices, Python ML services, and plant-edge systems. The ERP story is not a provider EHR story: do not substitute Epic, Meditech Expanse, or Mirth Connect unless those are explicitly uploaded later.

Northstar value story for first 90 days: use the $1.15B IT budget, $420M ERP/TSA exit envelope, $310M application operations/AMS envelope, and $100M-$120M tariff and margin headwind as the forcing-function context. Best first moves are evidence-led ERP/TSA sequencing, legacy app and AMS renegotiation leverage, QMS evidence automation, and clinical coding AI modernization with regulatory guardrails.
